Today, William went to the basketball court. Between what times could they have gone?
We know that:
William woke up at 7am.
Lisa saw William stretching at a yoga studio from 11am to 2pm.
John saw William walking towards the Statue of Liberty from 2pm to 3pm.
Sean saw William reading at the library from 3pm to 5pm.
Sarah saw William driving to the water park from 5pm to 9pm.
The basketball court was closed after 9pm.
Between what times could William have gone to the basketball court?

Options:
(A) 5pm to 9pm
(B) 3pm to 5pm
(C) 7am to 11am
(D) 11am to 2pm

Think step by step about the question. Keep reasoning concise (under 300 words). Then give your final answer on the last line in exactly this format: Answer: (X)
cot:

1. William woke up at 7am.
2. From 11am to 2pm, he was at a yoga studio.
3. From 2pm to 3pm, he was walking towards the Statue of Liberty.
4. From 3pm to 5pm, he was reading at the library.
5. From 5pm to 9pm, he was driving to the water park.
6. The basketball court was closed after 9pm.

Given these points, we can see that the only time William was not occupied and the basketball court was open (before it closed at 9pm) was between 3pm and 5pm. However, William was reading at the library during this time, so he couldn't have gone to the basketball court then.

The only other time frame when William was not occupied and the basketball court was open is between 2pm and 3pm. During this time, William was walking towards the Statue of Liberty, so he couldn't have gone to the basketball court then either.

The only remaining time frame when William was not occupied and the basketball court was open is between 11am and 2pm. During this time, William was at the yoga studio, so he couldn't have gone to the basketball court then.

The only time frame when William was not occupied and the basketball court was open is between 7am and 11am. During this time, William was just waking up, so it is a plausible time for him to have gone to the basketball court.

Answer: (C) 7am to 11am
